about: Who owns what. A role is the reason, the knowledge and what the work looks like in application. A user is assigned to a role. The user starts the role's agents; the agents and their sub-agents run the workflows to the end; the role's number says whether it worked. Brand-agnostic: no brand, person, price or target lives here. Targets and who fills each role live in each brand's roles.json.

chain.name: Owner
chain.does: Points the system and reviews what goes out

chain.name: Role
chain.does: Reason, knowledge, what good looks like, one number

chain.name: Holder
chain.does: The person or agent the role is given to

chain.name: Agent
chain.does: Runs the role's components start to finish

chain.name: Sub-agents
chain.does: One per step inside a component

chain.name: Workflow
chain.does: The components that make one type, in order

chain.name: Number
chain.does: The one result the role owns

chain.name: Loop
chain.does: The number changes the next round

split.rule: Agents do the work. People hold the taste and the calls. A person is added only where a call cannot be written as a check.

card.asks: What does the work look like when it is done?
Which one number does it own?
Which components does its agent run?
Which calls stay with a person?
What does it decide alone, and what goes to its lead?
Which of the owner's calls does it reach?
What does the number change next?

rules: Every number has one owner. Two owners is no owner.
A role owns an outcome, not a task list.
A role is named by what it does, never by who holds it.
A person or agent can hold several roles. A role can have several holders; the first one answers for its number.
After a hand-off the holder runs everything. The owner is asked only for his four calls.
The owner enters a workflow only when a trip-wire fires.
Authority grows when the number is hit and shrinks when it is missed.

authority.name: Act now
authority.scope: Anything inside the written process and the daily budget

authority.name: Decide and log
authority.scope: Direction inside the role's own function, written down the same day

authority.name: Propose, then proceed
authority.scope: Past the role's budget or across roles. Goes ahead after one working day unless stopped

authority.name: Owner decides
authority.scope: Cannot be undone, spends past the cap, goes live, signs, or changes positioning

rhythm.what: New brief: targets reset from actuals

naming.rule: A role id is lowercase with dashes and says the job.
One name everywhere: folder, path, command, button, lane and shared drive.
Who holds a role is one setting, never part of a name.
A stage is a component's place in a workflow. A stage is held by a role.
A hand-off is one folder and the work comes back inside it.
Stage words come from the one stage list.
Reuse a name that exists before making a new one.

calls.rule: The only decisions that are the owner's. Everything else in a role runs without him.
calls.grant: A call can be handed to a role for one brand. A grant is the owner's own act, written in that brand's roles.json. Nothing in the toolkit sets one.
